newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds slip back, outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds slip back, outlook positive.

text.p: *Australian bonds slipped back from the day's highs on profit-taking, but the set-back is expected to be short-lived, and technically this week's rally remains solid.
*Moody's review of Victoria, W. Australia has no impact.
Australian bond prices slipped back from the day's highs on profit-taking, but the set-back is expected to be short-lived, and technically this week's rally remains solid.

Long-dated yields fell to their lowest level in 2-1/2 years in early trading as the market factored in Thursday's further advance in U.S. Treasuries and after steady offshore and technical hedge fund buying, traders said.
However, this was quickly met by profit-taking domestic institutions, and in a relatively thin market, sellers won the day, they added.

The December 10-year bond futures contract sprinted to 92.280 just after the opening, the highest level for a front position since March 1994, but even though it was on the defensive thereafter it held key support at 92.210 at the close.
At the futures high the cash yield got below 7.75 percent.

Underpinning the market was a further dual currency samurai bond issue by Queensland Treasury Corp and the vague possibility that the RBA could ease policy at next week's board meeting, although most analysts see this move occuring in November.
However, news that Moody's may upgrade the Victorian and Western Australian states has already been discounted.

Yield spreads to other dollar bloc bonds turn mixed after an initial tightening trend. This most notable move was against New Zealand debt which rebounded after its June quarter GDP grew just 0.3 percent, the lowest quarterly rise since September 1992.

The 92.210 level on the 10-year bond represents the now breached peak seen in August. A sustained break below this level should find some support at 92.110, but then there is a chart gap to fill to around 92.075, analysts added.
